title: Automated Chloroform-Methanol Protein Extraction on the Biomek-FX Liquid Handler System
author: Yan Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3gsqjwe
materials: Open Biomek Software that controls Biomek-FX liquid handler system. Under "File" drop-down, click "Open" to select the automation method "Modular Protein Extraction method." Because different deck orientations and system components are possible, you will need to modify the method file (attached in the 'Before start' section) for your specific Biomek liquid handler system.

Because different deck orientations and system components are possible, you will need to modify the method file (attached in the 'Before start' section) for your specific Biomek liquid handler system.

steps.title: Initialize instrument and deck
steps.instruction: Click "Instrument Setup" under the "Setup" group node to view deck‑setup instructions, then arrange all labware on the deck as shown in the deck‑setup picture.

steps.title: Start protocol run
steps.instruction: Click the green "Run" button to begin the Biomek‑FX method.

steps.title: Add water and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Transfer 87.5 µL water from the water reservoir to the cell plate, then mix and resuspend the cell pellet with 20 pipetting cycles on the deck (the number of cycles is a user‑defined variable and may be changed).

steps.title: Transfer suspension to PCR plate
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire cell‑resuspension from the cell plate into the PCR96 plate.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Pause the protocol, then centrifuge the PCR96 plate at 2000 × g, 25 °C for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add methanol‑chloroform solvent
steps.instruction: Return the PCR96 plate to its deck position, swirl the 4:1 methanol:chloroform mixture in its reservoir to ensure it is well mixed, and pour the solvent into the reservoir.

steps.title: Remove first supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer 87 µL supernatant from the PCR96 plate back to the cell plate.

steps.title: Add solvent for lysis
steps.instruction: Transfer 125 µL of the 4:1 methanol:chloroform solvent to the PCR96 plate and mix with 20 pipetting cycles on the deck (cycles are user‑defined).

steps.title: Add water and seal
steps.instruction: Transfer 75 µL water into the PCR96 plate, seal the plate with a peelable seal using the microplate sealer, then gently invert the plate 5 times to mix.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Pause the protocol, centrifuge the sealed PCR96 plate at 4000 rpm, 25 °C for 2 minutes, then visually confirm that a clear protein pellet has formed in the middle; extend centrifugation time if needed.

steps.title: Remove second supernatant
steps.instruction: Return the PCR96 plate to the deck and transfer 170 µL of the top‑layer supernatant from the PCR96 plate to the cell plate.

steps.title: Add methanol and mix
steps.instruction: Add 75 µL methanol to the PCR96 plate and mix with 20 pipetting cycles on the deck (cycles are user‑defined).

steps.title: Third centrifugation
steps.instruction: Pause, visually verify that the chloroform layer has mixed well with the added methanol, then centrifuge the PCR96 plate at 4000 rpm, 25 °C for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Remove final supernatant
steps.instruction: Return the PCR96 plate to the deck and remove the remaining supernatant (volume not specified).

steps.title: Resuspend pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL of 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate containing 20 % methanol, mixing with a user‑defined number of pipetting cycles on the deck; note that samples are typically cloudy at this stage, may require additional mixing with a multichannel pipette, and the resuspension volume can be adjusted as needed.

steps.title: Store plate
steps.instruction: Store the PCR96 plate at –20 °C until ready for automated protein quantitation with the Biomek‑FX system.
